API Conventions Reference

Everything the last three slides established, collected in one place to check new endpoints against.

The previous three slides each introduced one piece of a convention. This slide is the reference itself — the short written summary this project follows for every endpoint from here on, not just the ones this lesson happens to touch.

Success responses always go through sendResource/sendCollection (Figure 3.1):

// A single resource — GET /tickets/:id, POST /tickets, PATCH /tickets/:id
{ "data": { "id": 1, "subject": "Cannot log in", "...": "..." } }

// A list — GET /tickets/:id/comments, GET /tags
{ "data": [ { "...": "..." }, { "...": "..." } ] }

// A list that supports pagination — GET /tickets (this lesson, later topic)
{ "data": [ "..." ], "meta": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 10, "total": 42, "totalPages": 5 } }

Error responses always go through the centralized error handler (Figures 3.2–3.4), never a controller's own res.status(...).json(...):

// Any error — a thrown ApiError, a failed validation, an unrecognised bug
{ "error": { "message": "Ticket 5 not found" } }

// A validation failure specifically also carries field-by-field detail
{ "error": { "message": "Validation failed", "details": [
  { "field": "customerId", "message": "Required" }
] } }

Status codes, applied consistently across Ticket/Comment/Tag:

Situation Status
Fetching or updating something that exists 200 OK
Creating something new 201 Created
Deleting something that exists 204 No Content (empty body)
The request body/params/query fail validation 400 Bad Request
The URL names something that doesn't exist 404 Not Found
The request conflicts with existing data (duplicate, still-referenced row) 409 Conflict
Anything unrecognised — a real bug, not a client mistake 500 Internal Server Error (generic message only)

Any new endpoint added later in this build is expected to fit into this same table rather than inventing its own response shape.
